subject: maths
question: Pipe X can fill a tank in 9 hours and Pipe Y can fill it in 21 hours. If they are opened on alternate hours and Pipe X is opened first, in how many hours shall the tank be full?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity = LCM of 9 and 21 = 63 units.

Efficiency of X = 7 units/hr, Y = 3 units/hr.

Work done in 1 cycle (2 hours) = 7 + 3 = 10 units.

In 6 cycles (12 hours), work done = 60 units, remaining = 3 units.

X fills the remaining 3 units in 3/7 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 ³/₇ hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe X = 9 hours

Time taken by Pipe Y = 21 hours

 X

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total work to be done = 63 units

⇒ Pipes are opened alternately starting with X.

⇒ Work done in 1st hour by X = 7 units

⇒ Work done in 2nd hour by Y = 3 units

⇒ Total work done in a 2-hour cycle = 7 + 3 = 10 units

⇒ In 6 cycles (12 hours), work done = 10 × 6 = 60 units

⇒ Remaining work = 63 − 60 = 3 units

⇒ In the 13th hour, it is Pipe X's turn.

⇒ Time taken by X to fill the remaining 3 units = 3 ÷ 7 hours

⇒ Total time taken = 12 + 3/7 = 12 ³/₇ hours

**∴ The correct answer is 12 ³/₇ hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternate Working Rule

When entities work on alternate hours or days, calculate the work done in one complete cycle, multiply to get closest to the total work, and assign the remaining work to the entity whose turn is next.

Pipes & Cisterns

It operates similarly to Time and Work problems. The total capacity of the tank acts as Total Work (LCM of individual times) and the rate of filling is the Efficiency.

Emptying Pipes

If a pipe empties the tank instead of filling it, its efficiency is taken as negative, reducing the overall net work done per cycle.
